The property is located at two intersections and is bounded by Victoria Street South to

The property is a combination of five separate individual residential properties.
The lands are currently used and occupied with four single detached dwellings and one
fourplex.
The lands immediately to the southeast are part of the Victoria Park Heritage Conservation
District and are used for low rise residential purposes.
The surrounding lands comprise a mix of low and medium residential land uses as well as
commercial uses.
In the City's urban structure, the subject property is identified as a Protected Major
Transit Station Area, or PMTSA.
PMTSAs are intended to be a focus for accommodating growth through development to support existing
and planned transit and rapid transit levels.
The lands are designated Strategic Growth Area A in the City's Official Plan, as recently
considered by Council and approved by the Region.
Growth Area A is generally intended to accommodate growth and development and intensification.
It is anticipated that the majority of development and or redevelopment in Strategic Growth Area
A will occur through infill, including missing middle housing and compatible non-residential
uses.
The lands are currently zoned low intensity mixed use corridor zone or MU1 in the City's
Zoning By-law 85 .
Since the subject property is within a PMTSA, under the Planning Act there are no parking
requirements.
Under By-law 85 , the owner has made application for a Zoning By-law amendment to change the
zoning from MU1 to MU2, medium intensity mixed use corridor zone, with a special regulation
provision as well as a holding provision.
The requested ZBA, Zoning By-law Amendment, would have the following main effects.
It would allow a building height, a maximum building height of 28.8 metres.
It would allow a maximum floor space ratio of 4.2.
It would prohibit geothermal energy systems and a holding provision would be added at
the request of the Region for a detailed noise study and associated implementation.
The lands are also zoned Strategic Growth Area 2 or SGA 2 as part of the Council approved
but appealed Growing Together bylaw.
Both zoning bylaws are applicable.
Under Bylaw 2019-051, which is the more recent zoning bylaw, the owner has made application
for a zoning bylaw amendment to change the, to retain the SGA 2 zone and to add a site-specific
provision and a holding provision.
The main effects of this zoning bylaw amendment are firstly to allow a maximum building height
within 7.5 metres of an SGA 1 zone or a low-rise residential zone to be 28.8 metres.
Also to allow a minimum yard setback for the 7th and 8th stories to be 4.0 metres from
a street line.
To not require a community or commercial use on the ground floor level.
To reduce the minimum percentage of street line ground floor facade openings.
And similarly to the 85 by-law to prohibit geothermal energy systems and require a noise
study through a holding provision.
The requested ZBA application would facilitate the proposed development concept which consists
of a mid-rise residential apartment building.
The building is proposed to have a height of 8 stories or 28.8 metres and would contain
approximately 120 units in a rental format.
The owner has stated that they are seeking CMHC funding and that would equate to 24 dwelling
units under the CMHC program. In addition the building would be subject to
inclusionary zoning requirements. Two percent of the building would be
required for affordable housing. 120 class A bicycle parking spaces would be
required. There would be amenity spaces on site. No service parking is proposed.
There's an opportunity here to facilitate the lands with missing middle
housing in a mid-rise built form. This would add 120 units to the
